No physical format/writer/history/RPC/UI acceptance is being claimed. This is the pure member prerequisite to future replay; no consumer exists in this export.

Changes: A-F1 refuses hash-valid original bytes disagreeing with authenticated lengths, before calling them corrupt. Referenced service request lengths must fit service::MAX_REQUEST. A-F2 preserves incomplete-copy membership rows/lengths in M1 but clears unauthenticated, membership-only expected lengths for availability/restoration semantics. Loss exposes recomputed Basis (IssuerMetadata, VerifiedCopyRecipe, UnverifiedMembership, OriginalObject). The signed unavailable wire still has its original four fields; a later full replay must recompute per-entry basis from the member and expose it in API/UI. No external copy-job authentication is invented; incomplete membership can have omitted/fabricated rows that remain explicitly unverified. A-F3 now rejects shared service-request CIDs even when bytes are missing, because exact request bytes fix one writer/operation/position. General raw framing still hashes what it receives and confers no authority. Metadata contradictions are not silently repaired.

The independent Python construction/loss oracle pins the changed interpretation and verifies newly added contradiction cases itself; it still explicitly is NOT a full second member-semantic validator. New fixtures are public scalar keys only. Promoted reviewer deterministic RP01..RP17 exclude timing RP10b/c/d; RP02/03/14 expectations deliberately change to the corrected contract. Raw reviewer originals remain unchanged. Three author probes additionally cover false authenticated orphan length, exact membership-byte charging, and orphan hash mismatch. Rust framing now has é*40/é*41 edges and corrected source provenance. No non-test framing code changes.

Verify before/after exact manifest paths/SHA256 AND Git blobs at the pinned commit, using explicit repo /Users/m/code/kan-tools/kan/.worktrees/kan-v2-recovery-member; discovery from this export would find the parent. Only initial extra north-star.json; put ALL commands/raw logs/probes/mutations/failed methods and final REPORT.txt under review-evidence/. Restore tracked bytes and remove temporary probe copies after running. No parent edits/Git writes, installs, .lake/own target, network/live archives/keys/traffic or unrelated process kills. Do not run revert_v2.py from this export. One heavy job at a time; use shared CARGO_TARGET_DIR, 4 jobs, cargo clean -p kan first.

Reproduce bounded baseline: v2-crypto tests evidence_recovery_member, evidence_recovery_member_review_regressions, evidence_recovery_member_corrections and evidence_recovery_commitment_review_regressions; strict all-target v2 Clippy, fmt and Python member fixture --check. Read the author's retained correction qualification logs including failed lint attempt. Reproduce selected relevant correction controls and whole-production-file reversion with API-compatible tests/evidence_recovery_member_corrections.rs (no use of newly added Basis), retaining honest semantic versus diagnostic classification. Use git show at 8ddefda for old member source if needed, explicitly against the named repo; restore afterwards. Independently probe the changed trust/length/CID rules, not only the author tests. Reuse unchanged earlier review evidence rather than rerunning 27+17 historical controls, wall-clock timing probes or unrelated large matrices; broaden only for a concrete new concern.

Write a full requirement/evidence/finding report with one hard APPROVE / APPROVE WITH FOLLOW-UPS / REDIRECT / BLOCK verdict. Identify anything that must be resolved before replay consumes this component. Keep all parent bundle/frontend criteria open, and don't round pure correction qualification up to end-to-end delivery.

set -u
umask 077
root=/Users/m/code/kan-tools/kan/.worktrees/kan-v2-recovery-member
cd "$root/.local-state/reviews/member-corrections" || exit 1
export CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/Users/m/code/kan-tools/kan/.worktrees/kan-v2-library-resilience/.local-state/target
export CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4 CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=0 CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG=0 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0
export KAN_CRYPTO_ORACLE_PYTHON=/Users/m/code/kan-tools/kan/.worktrees/kan-v2-encryption/.local-state/crypto-oracle-env/bin/python
export KAN_TLS_ORACLE_PYTHON=/opt/homebrew/bin/python3
export GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=commit.gpgsign GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=false
/opt/homebrew/bin/claude -p --safe-mode --model claude-opus-5-5 --effort medium --no-session-persistence --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config '{"mcpServers":{}}' --permission-mode dontAsk --tools 'Bash,Read,Glob,Grep,Write' --allowedTools Bash Read Glob Grep Write --output-format stream-json --verbose < "$root/.local-state/reviews/member-corrections-prompt.txt" > "$root/.local-state/reviews/member-corrections.jsonl" 2> "$root/.local-state/reviews/member-corrections.stderr"
review_exit=$?
printf '%s\n' "$review_exit" > "$root/.local-state/reviews/member-corrections.exit"
exit "$review_exit"

## Read first, in order

3. `docs/ROADMAP.md` — the current shipped baseline, active RFC 3 issue graph,

   network phases redirected to the current roadmap.

## The one non-negotiable invariant
The fold reads morphisms; it never mutates objects. **No operation destroys a
subject.** Identity and status are computed objects (path-spaces / posets),
collapsed to flat values only at the display boundary, never in the store.
If a change would let one actor's write mutate or destroy another's data, it's wrong.

## What to build first (the spine — do NOT build the cathedral)
Local-only, one human, one-or-more local agents, one repo, no sync:
Claim + DAG-CBOR CID + signing → local append-only log (source of truth) →
disposable SQLite index → the fold (identity-before-state, same enrichment,
decategorify only at render) → git anchors + computable relation providers →
CLI + MCP server with budgeted context assembly.

Explicitly OUT for the local spine: sync/atproto/lexicons, TUI, web dashboard,
editor extensions, >2 trust enrichments, enforcement hooks, incremental fold.
The local-only spine shipped through v0.3.0-beta.1. Do not treat that historical
scope fence as an open-ended ban or use ADR-35's old version table as the
current plan. Read `docs/ROADMAP.md` first for sync-adjacent work; public
ATProto publication is governed by RFC 3 (currently Review) and issues
#235–#241 under epic #29. The older sync staging design remains context for the
separate HostedRelay track.

## House rules
- Rust. Use `atproto-repo` + `atproto-dasl` for MST/CAR/CID (`atrium-crypto`
  for signing), so local-only and future atproto are the same on-disk
  artifact. **Not** `atrium-repo` — ADR-1 originally picked it, but ADR-11
  found a confirmed data-loss bug in its MST (filed upstream:
  atrium-rs/atrium#343) and ADR-12 records the switch. Before trusting any
  storage-layer crate here again, run **both** checks before building on it,
  not after:
  1. **Reachability** (ADR-11/12) — sequential inserts, check full
     reachability after every single one, not just at the end.
  2. **Conformance** (ADR-90) — compare the artifact against an *independent
     implementation*, not against our own reading of the spec. Reachability
     alone is not enough: `atproto-repo` 0.14.5's MST never split, losing
     nothing while writing a repo no conformant implementation agrees with
     (kan#204) — a quadratic write cliff and a wrong root CID that the
     reachability rule passes cleanly. `tests/mst_conformance.rs` is the
     working example; `src/mst/` is what it cost — kan now owns the MST
     outright, because a `[patch.crates-io]` fix reaches CI but never reaches
     `cargo install kan`.
- Correctness before performance. The reference fold recomputes; caching and
  incremental folds are follow-ups, optimized only against passing fixtures.
- A persistence change is also a surface-contract change. Update
  `tests/fixtures/read-write-surface.tsv`, the typed capability at the mutation
  site, and `tests/surface_conformance.rs` together; derived media never become
  authority merely because they are persisted or fast.

  surfaces in the graph as data. Do NOT port crosslink's blocking hooks.
- One surface: CLI + MCP for v1. The owner explicitly authorized a v2 operator
  front end on 2026-10-18: `.design/kan-v2-operations.md`. It reads the same
  operations API as the CLI; this exception does not add a workflow authority.
- Provenance is sacred: never fabricate or drop `cites` edges.

The local-only path must be *dramatically* simpler than the multi-actor path
(one log, all subjects Local, no SameAs stitching, no contest stage, latest-wins).

Declared in four AX-driven phases ([`ADR-0032`](adrs/32-verb-lexicon-reorganized-by-ax-phase-mcp-tool-surface-catches-up-to-the.md)) — `kan --help`
reflects this order directly, so treat it as the source of truth over this

- Recording: `observe | plan | decide | block | resolve | result`
- Structuring: `same | relate | mark`
- Correcting: `retract | reject`
- Recalling: `show | status | issues | context [--budget N]`

`Anchor`/`RelationKind` variant, or is a pure read/fold over the claim graph

213	rules you derived and from where.

261	```

265	here.

267	**A round of fixes to a BLOCK gets its own review** — kan's ADR-52, stated here

269	validated **eight times** in this repo, and three times consecutively in one
270	milestone, where each round found defects the previous round's author could not

282	fail, restore, watch it pass. A round that says "fixed and the suite is green"

286	## Rules

289	  against the real log appends real claims — that is how a junk
290	  `telos/review-probe` subject ended up in day's own record and then in its
291	  session-start context. Probe in a scratch repo, or retract in the same
292	  breath. An assessment that pollutes the record it assesses is measuring its
293	  own footprint.
294	- **Check the other side of every interface.** The most serious finding this
295	  review has produced was a hook wired to an event whose stdout never reaches
296	  the model — invisible to every test, because the tests asserted what the
297	  tool printed rather than whether anything read it. Read the docs for the
298	  thing being integrated with; do not infer its behavior from your own side.
299	- Do NOT modify code. This atom reads and judges; fixing is a separate atom.
300	- Do NOT trust the design doc, the ADRs, or the commit messages about whether
301	  the work was done. They are claims about the work, not the work.
302	- Do NOT report a command as run if you did not run it.
303	- Every finding cites a file path and line, or command output.
304	- If the design doc itself is wrong or incoherent, say that — auditing against a
305	  bad specification faithfully is still a failed review.

### Step 3 — Verify the evidence yourself

Run the project's own verification, in this order, and report raw results:

1. Build (`cargo build --workspace --all-targets`, `npm run build`, `make`, …)
2. Tests (`cargo test --workspace`, `npm test`, …)
3. Lint (`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, …)
4. Format (`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, …)

If a claimed test exists, **run that specific test and confirm it fails when the
behavior is broken** where you can do so cheaply. A test that passes
unconditionally is not coverage. If you cannot run something, say so — do not
report unrun commands as passing.

### Step 4 — Scope-narrowing check

Grep the diff, the design doc, and any new decision records for scope-narrowing
language: `out of scope`, `deferred`, `follow-up`, `future work`, `for now`,
`TODO`, `later`, `v2`.

Judge each instance independently:

- **Legitimate**: named before implementation, recorded, and genuinely separable.
- **Suspicious**: narrowed *during* implementation, or narrowing exactly the part
  that was hard, or deferring the requirement that made the feature worth doing.

Quote each instance and give a verdict per instance. A design that ended up
smaller than it started is not automatically wrong, but it needs to have been
decided, not drifted into.

### Step 5 — Forbidden-pattern re-introduction

Check the diff against this repo's own stated house rules — the ones in its
`CLAUDE.md` and its decision records, not generic best practice. For kan and day
specifically, that includes:

- The fold reads; it never mutates. No operation destroys a subject.
- Affordance, not enforcement — no blocking hooks, no gates on agent action.
- One surface (CLI + MCP); no second UI sneaking in.
- Provenance is sacred: `cites` edges are never fabricated or dropped.
- day stores nothing of its own; durable state is kan claims.

For any other repo, derive the equivalent list from its own docs and say which
rules you derived and from where.

### Step 6 — Verdict

End with **exactly one** of these four, in bold, with a one-paragraph rationale:

- **APPROVE** — requirements met, evidence verified independently, no drift.
- **APPROVE WITH FOLLOW-UPS** — sound and shippable; specific, named gaps that
  do not undermine the north star. List them as concrete follow-ups.
- **REDIRECT** — the work is competent but pointed somewhere other than the
  stated telos. Say precisely where it diverged and what it should serve instead.
- **BLOCK** — a correctness, safety, or invariant violation. Name the invariant
  and the exact code that violates it.

Do not soften the verdict to be agreeable. Do not inflate it to seem rigorous.
"APPROVE" on genuinely good work is a useful signal that only stays useful if
you are willing to say it.

### Step 7 — Record it

```bash
day review record <subject> \
  --verdict APPROVE-WITH-FOLLOW-UPS \
  --rationale "<one line>" \
  --cites <cid of the design/plan claim being audited>
```

The verdict must be one of the four values above and must cite the claim it
audits; `day` rejects anything else rather than recording a verdict nobody can
trace back to what it judged.

Record each material finding as its own claim citing that verdict, so a later
session can find the finding without re-reading this whole review:

```bash
kan observe "<finding>" --subject <subject> --cites "$VERDICT"
```

If the verdict is BLOCK or REDIRECT, also mark the subject:

```bash
kan mark <subject> --value Blocked   # check `kan mark --help` for valid values
```

### Step 8 — What comes next

```bash
day next adversarial-review
```

Report what the graph says rather than naming a step from memory. A project
that loops review back into design has declared that; another may terminate
here.

**A round of fixes to a BLOCK gets its own review** — kan's ADR-52, stated here
rather than left as something a person has to remember. It has now been
validated **eight times** in this repo, and three times consecutively in one
milestone, where each round found defects the previous round's author could not
see. The severity moved as it went: round 1 found code defects, round 2 found a
bug the round-1 fix introduced, and round 3 found that *"the code changes in this
round are correct… what is wrong is the evidence."*

So when this review returns BLOCK, the fixes are a new implementation, not an
addendum to the reviewed one, and they are reviewed as such. The author of a fix
round is the least able person to see what it missed, which is the same argument
that makes this atom cold in the first place (Step 0).

If the fix round closes a finding, its commit carries a `Demonstrated-by:`
trailer from `scripts/revert-demo.py` — revert the fix, watch the named test
fail, restore, watch it pass. A round that says "fixed and the suite is green"
has asserted the weaker of the two things, and day#116's first instance is a fix
whose entire reversion left 337/337 tests passing.

## Rules

- **Probes leave traces.** Verifying a defect by running the real command
  against the real log appends real claims — that is how a junk
  `telos/review-probe` subject ended up in day's own record and then in its
  session-start context. Probe in a scratch repo, or retract in the same
  breath. An assessment that pollutes the record it assesses is measuring its
  own footprint.
- **Check the other side of every interface.** The most serious finding this
  review has produced was a hook wired to an event whose stdout never reaches
  the model — invisible to every test, because the tests asserted what the
  tool printed rather than whether anything read it. Read the docs for the
  thing being integrated with; do not infer its behavior from your own side.
- Do NOT modify code. This atom reads and judges; fixing is a separate atom.
- Do NOT trust the design doc, the ADRs, or the commit messages about whether
  the work was done. They are claims about the work, not the work.
- Do NOT report a command as run if you did not run it.
- Every finding cites a file path and line, or command output.
- If the design doc itself is wrong or incoherent, say that — auditing against a
  bad specification faithfully is still a failed review.

"""Verify the export against the frozen manifest and against Git blobs at the pinned commit.

usage: python3 -I identity_check.py <export_dir> <manifest.json> <repo> <label>
Read-only: uses `git -C <repo> ls-tree -r` and `git cat-file --batch`; no Git writes.
"""
import hashlib
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys

export, manifest_path, repo, label = sys.argv[1:5]
ALLOWED_EXTRA_TOP = {"north-star.json", "review-evidence"}

manifest = json.load(open(manifest_path))
commit = manifest["commit"]
files = manifest["files"]
problems = []


def sha(path):
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        for chunk in iter(lambda: f.read(1 << 20), b""):
            h.update(chunk)
    return h.hexdigest()


# 1. export vs manifest
on_disk = set()
for root, dirs, names in os.walk(export):
    rel_root = os.path.relpath(root, export)
    if rel_root == ".":
        dirs[:] = [d for d in dirs if d not in ALLOWED_EXTRA_TOP]
    for n in names:
        rel = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(rel_root, n))
        if rel in ALLOWED_EXTRA_TOP:
            continue
        on_disk.add(rel)
missing = sorted(set(files) - on_disk)
extra = sorted(on_disk - set(files))
mismatch = sorted(p for p in files if p in on_disk and sha(os.path.join(export, p)) != files[p])
problems += [f"missing {p}" for p in missing] + [f"extra {p}" for p in extra] + [f"sha {p}" for p in mismatch]

# 2. manifest vs git tree at the pinned commit (read-only plumbing)
head = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", repo, "rev-parse", "HEAD"], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
tree = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", repo, "ls-tree", "-r", "-z", commit], capture_output=True).stdout
entries = {}
for rec in tree.split(b"\0"):
    if not rec:
        continue
    meta, path = rec.split(b"\t", 1)
    mode, typ, oid = meta.split()
    entries[path.decode()] = (mode.decode(), typ.decode(), oid.decode())
not_in_tree = sorted(set(files) - set(entries))
not_in_manifest = sorted(set(entries) - set(files))
problems += [f"manifest-not-in-tree {p}" for p in not_in_tree] + [f"tree-not-in-manifest {p}" for p in not_in_manifest]

blob_mismatch = []
proc = subprocess.Popen(["git", "-C", repo, "cat-file", "--batch"], stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE)
for p in sorted(set(files) & set(entries)):
    mode, typ, oid = entries[p]
    if typ != "blob":
        problems.append(f"non-blob {p} {typ}")
        continue
    proc.stdin.write(oid.encode() + b"\n")
    proc.stdin.flush()
    header = proc.stdout.readline().split()
    size = int(header[2])
    data = proc.stdout.read(size)
    proc.stdout.read(1)
    if mode == "120000":
        # symlink: compare link target bytes
        local = os.readlink(os.path.join(export, p)).encode() if os.path.islink(os.path.join(export, p)) else None
        if local != data:
            blob_mismatch.append(p)
        continue
    if hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest() != files[p]:
        blob_mismatch.append(p)
proc.stdin.close()
proc.wait()
problems += [f"blob {p}" for p in blob_mismatch]

top_extras = sorted(n for n in os.listdir(export) if n in ALLOWED_EXTRA_TOP)
print(f"[{label}] commit={commit} repo_HEAD={head} manifest_files={len(files)} export_files_checked={len(on_disk)} "
      f"git_tree_entries={len(entries)} blob_mismatches={len(blob_mismatch)}")
print(f"[{label}] extras_allowed_present={top_extras}")
print(f"[{label}] problems={len(problems)}")
for p in problems[:200]:
    print(f"[{label}]   {p}")
sys.exit(1 if problems else 0)

1	INDEPENDENT ADVERSARIAL REVIEW — recovery-member export, pinned 5e54513c629b3b2e954eff5e3e43f98d471725c0
2	Reviewer: Claude Code, Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5), fresh cold session, no subagents, did not author this code.
3	Scope A: logical recovery-member verifier (3169a0a, merged in 88db7c9, docs 5e54513).
4	Scope B: framing review follow-through (99f1fba), relative to .design/reviews/kan-v2-recovery-commitment-opus/evidence/REPORT.txt.
5	
6	=====================================================================================================
7	CUSTODY AND METHOD
8	- Integrity (logs/manifest-pre.txt, logs/manifest-post.txt; script cmd/verify_manifest.py):
9	  - The export tree was compared to ../recovery-member-identity.json: exactly 3108 files, sha256 each.
10	  - The identity was compared to the git blobs at 5e54513, using explicit `git -C <worktree>` (ls-tree plus
11	    cat-file --batch content sha256). No discovery from the export was used.
12	  - Result: pre 0 problems, post 0 problems, blob mismatches 0. The only extras were north-star.json and
13	    review-evidence/. Repo HEAD equals the pinned commit.
14	- Every command is logged in COMMANDS.txt with its exit code and elapsed time; raw output is in logs/.
15	- Environment:
16	  - CARGO_TARGET_DIR was the shared .../kan-v2-library-resilience/.local-state/target, with CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4
17	    and --offline.
18	  - `cargo clean -p kan` was run first (logs/01). One heavy job ran at a time. No own target, no installs.
19	- Probes and mutations:
20	  - Temporary probe files were placed in tests/ only while they ran. They were confirmed cmp-identical to
21	    review-evidence/probes/ and then removed (COMMANDS.txt TEMP-PLACE/TEMP-REMOVE).
22	  - Every source mutation was restored and its sha256 checked against the frozen manifest after each case.
23	- What I did not do:
24	  - No git writes, no parent edits, no kan/day writes, no network, no keys, no live archives.
25	  - revert_v2.py was not run.
26	- Recording: git-first (day#168/kan#197). `day review record` / `kan observe` were deliberately NOT run. This
27	  file is the record.
28	- Exploratory read-only commands (file reads, greps, git show/diff) are not all individually logged;
29	  every claim in this report cites a re-runnable log or a file:line.
30	- One combined cleanup command (rm + baseline + manifest + parent `git status`) was denied by the harness
31	  permission mode. I re-ran the steps individually; all succeeded except that parent `git status` was not
32	  retried.
33	  - Integrity is instead established by the manifest + blob check above.
34	- North star: from the supplied north-star.json, kan was not queried.
35	  - telos/raw-data-and-projections (live Decision bafyreied3…): "Raw attested data is retained in full and
36	    never collapsed in the store. Every simplification … is a determined projection computed on demand…"
37	  - The export notes excluded_by_trust: 2. Those claims were not reconstructed.
38	  - This work serves that telos directly. It retains corrupt/empty/orphan original bytes verbatim in M1, and
39	    "loss" is a projection over them. The tension with telos/performance-at-scale is visible only as bounded
40	    work limits.
41	
42	=====================================================================================================
43	BASELINE (reproduced, not trusted; logs/02-07 initial, logs/90-94 final after restoration; identical)
44	- `cargo test --features v2-crypto` with --test evidence_recovery_member, evidence_recovery_commitment,
45	  evidence_recovery_commitment_review_regressions and evidence_recovery_observation:
46	  - 16 + 8 + 2 + 7 = 33 passed, 0 failed.

48	- `cargo clippy --features v2-crypto --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
49	- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.

51	  - recovery_member_vectors.py --check: "16 independently constructed member cases; all constructed issuer
52	    chains independently verified".
53	  - recovery_commitments.py --check: 9 member/output and 4 restoration vectors.
54	- These match the author's claim of 33 + 2, clippy/fmt clean and fixture regeneration.
55	- The Python builder imports only cryptography / hashlib / the attestation and framing oracles. It calls no
56	  cargo or subprocess.
57	  - It builds real canonical signed JSON requests (public scalars 3/4/5/6) and verifies every issuer proof with
58	    its own attestation verifier.
59	  - Rust then verifies the Python-signed writer requests: verifiedRequests 3 in the intact cases. That is
60	    cross-implementation evidence for writer signatures.
61	  - It is honestly NOT a semantic verifier. losses() does no length-conflict or writer checks, and it labels
62	    itself that way.

64	=====================================================================================================
65	A. LOGICAL RECOVERY-MEMBER VERIFIER (src/evidence_recovery_member.rs, 552 lines; read in full)
66	
67	Code facts used below:
68	- verify() takes an owner Context plus borrowed slices (:76-82). It has no fs/SQLite/rusqlite use; grep finds
69	  none. Its only consumer is a lib.rs:32 module declaration.
70	- Item cap is checked in Work::new (:137) before any map/vec allocation. Input-byte charges come before each
71	  decode/hash (:262, :277, :303, :436).
72	- Hashing polls per 64 KiB (:168-174). There are cancel/deadline polls around each record and each writer
73	  verification (:411, :459, :484, :494, :543).
74	- Framing receives the remaining duration and the shared cancel flag (:501-509).
75	- Per-writer chain (:355-364), unique (writer, op) (:366-369), single entry and slot == SHA-256(op)
76	  (:373-390), purpose by range (:320-331), historical receipt issuer (:332-342), static writer (:344-354).
77	- Source digest (:290-295, :398-407, :413-429) is byte-identical in recipe to src/evidence_store/copied.rs:148-198.
78	- Object validity = nonempty && known length matches && hash matches (:447-454).
79	- Writer verification runs only for Available occurrences (:461-473). Null coordinates cover unreferenced
80	  non-available keys (:483-493).
81	- Member has private fields and getters only (:98-125). It has no publication, history or durability surface.
82	- Manifest/receipt schemas are closed with all fields required (src/evidence.rs:463-522), so the Ipld
83	  indexing at :341-378 cannot hit a missing key.

- The Python builder imports only cryptography / hashlib / the attestation and framing oracles. It calls no
  cargo or subprocess.
  - It builds real canonical signed JSON requests (public scalars 3/4/5/6) and verifies every issuer proof with

A. LOGICAL RECOVERY-MEMBER VERIFIER (src/evidence_recovery_member.rs, 552 lines; read in full)

Code facts used below:
- verify() takes an owner Context plus borrowed slices (:76-82). It has no fs/SQLite/rusqlite use; grep finds
  none. Its only consumer is a lib.rs:32 module declaration.
- Item cap is checked in Work::new (:137) before any map/vec allocation. Input-byte charges come before each
  decode/hash (:262, :277, :303, :436).
- Hashing polls per 64 KiB (:168-174). There are cancel/deadline polls around each record and each writer
  verification (:411, :459, :484, :494, :543).
- Framing receives the remaining duration and the shared cancel flag (:501-509).
- Per-writer chain (:355-364), unique (writer, op) (:366-369), single entry and slot == SHA-256(op)
  (:373-390), purpose by range (:320-331), historical receipt issuer (:332-342), static writer (:344-354).
- Source digest (:290-295, :398-407, :413-429) is byte-identical in recipe to src/evidence_store/copied.rs:148-198.
- Object validity = nonempty && known length matches && hash matches (:447-454).
- Writer verification runs only for Available occurrences (:461-473). Null coordinates cover unreferenced
  non-available keys (:483-493).
- Member has private fields and getters only (:98-125). It has no publication, history or durability surface.
- Manifest/receipt schemas are closed with all fields required (src/evidence.rs:463-522), so the Ipld
  indexing at :341-378 cannot hit a missing key.

Reviewer probes (probes/zz_review_member_probes.rs: 16 tests; probes/zz_review_member_probes2.rs: 4 tests).
On the unmodified tree all pass (logs/13, logs/14). Observations:
- RP01: an unreferenced staged membership key in a COMPLETE copy gets exactly one null coordinate with its
  authenticated length.
  - Missing gives missing; tampered gives corrupt.
  - Combined order is [occ1 corrupt, occ2 missing, null staged missing], as codec :168-170 requires.
- RP02 (characterisation): a PARTIAL profile-3 copy accepts membership that no digest authenticates.
  - A fabricated key with length 77 is reported as a null "missing" loss with expectedLength 77.
  - Silently dropping a staged key is accepted.
  - Re-lengthening a staged key turns valid bytes into "corrupt".
  - The same fabrication in a complete copy refuses with "source metadata digest".
- RP03: two occurrences sharing one request CID are accepted, with bytes missing, as two "missing" losses.
  Supplying the genuine bytes then refuses with "retained writer request". No bytes can ever satisfy it.
- RP04: retained receipts from the current issuer instead of the plan's historical issuer refuse with
  "historical receipt issuer", with bytes present or missing.
- RP05: a plan tip at a non-final manifest, with a correct digest, refuses with "source tip".
- RP06: plan target scope or issuer differing from the owner context refuses with "plan binding". Archive

- RP07: admitted purpose inside the retained range refuses with "proof purpose". The mixed case refuses with
  "historical receipt issuer" first; the codec says diagnostic precedence is not contract.
- RP08: reversed, duplicate or DAG-CBOR membership refuses. Profile-2 membership refuses, as does profile 3
  without a plan.
- RP09: the record schema already refuses non-static did:key writers. For did:web+documentCid and
  did:plc+versionId writers with bytes missing, the verifier refuses with "static writer".
- RP10a: pre-cancelled with a later broken proof gives Cancelled.
- RP10b (timing): cancel at 20% of a 64 MiB member stage (~1.7 s) gives Cancelled after 0.3–1.1 ms.
- RP10c: a deadline of 342 ms returned Budget at 343.5 ms.
- RP10d (timing, finer): worst cancel latency over 6 offsets was 1.15 ms, against a 106 ms single 4 MiB hash.
- RP11: items=0, or input_bytes one below a 4 MiB object, gives Budget; the exact amount is accepted.
- RP12: wrong owner scope or issuer gives "issuer proof". A non-canonical observer gives "issuer encoding".
  A same-key observer is accepted, per the recorded decision.
- RP13: the DASL parser refuses uppercase CID text, so a typed Cid cannot carry a non-canonical spelling.
- RP14a (characterisation): the GENUINE hash-valid signed request bytes are present, but the
  issuer-re-signed manifest length is n+1. Result: the member is ACCEPTED, verified_requests=0 and the loss
  is {occ 1, expectedLength n+1, Corrupt}. See finding A-F1.
- RP14b: the empty-bytes CID referenced with signed length 1, with the empty row present, is accepted as
  Corrupt.
- RP15: an empty orphan keyed by the empty-bytes CID gives a null Corrupt loss.
- RP16: a partial copy with a retained reference absent from membership (bytes missing) refuses.
- RP17: a broken writer chain with bytes missing refuses with "writer predecessor".

Compiled guard-removal controls (cmd/controls.py; mutations/*.txt; kill messages in logs/21 and logs/23).
- Reproduction of the author's 9:
  - 8 are killed with semantic assertions, i.e. Ok where a refusal was due, or a wrong loss vector:
    item-budget, input-budget, source-digest, expected-length, duplicate-operation, original-hash,
    orphan-loss, writer-signature.
  - A-expected-length: its kills in the owner_pins test and the conflicting-membership Python case are
    LABEL-ONLY, because the source digest still refuses. The semantic kill is the profile-2 shared-CID test
    (left: None).
  - A-cancelled (EXPLICIT AUTHOR SURVIVOR, retained) still PASSES the entire author suite, as the author
    recorded. That suite is not evidence of prompt interruption. My probes kill it:
    - RP10a: Invalid("issuer proof") instead of Cancelled, i.e. semantic work ran after cancellation.
    - RP10b: latency 1.40 s against a 1.75 s member stage.
    - RP10d: worst 388 ms against a 110 ms object hash.
- Reviewer controls:
  - Semantic kills found ONLY by reviewer probes (the author suite survives each):
    - R01 historical receipt issuer (RP04)
    - R02 source tip (RP05)
    - R08 null coordinates for membership keys (RP01, RP02)
    - R10 static writer (RP09)
    - R11 plan scope/issuer binding (RP06)
    - R12 hash unchunked and R13 no per-chunk poll (RP10d, timing; worst 82–85 ms against a ~110 ms hash)
    - R17 non-empty validity rule (RP15)
  - Author-suite LABEL-ONLY, semantic only with reviewer probes:
    - R05 retained-reference membership. The author tests use complete copies, where the digest refuses; RP16
      partial gives left: None.
    - R09 writer predecessor. The author test has bytes present, so the writer request refuses; RP17 with
      bytes missing gives left: None.
  - Semantic kills by the author suite:
    - R04 service slot
    - R06 partial untracked object
    - R07 proof purpose (via the Python profile-2 retained-purpose vector)
    - R16 full-flag
  - Label-only, layered: R18 record position. The issuer-proof chain refuses first, and MemberFraming.record
    re-checks contiguity.
  - SURVIVORS:
    - R03 slot-conflict map: an EQUIVALENT/redundant guard. slot = SHA-256(op), and (writer, op) is already
      unique (:366-369), so (writer, slot) can never recur without a hash collision.
    - R14 the initial poll in Work::new: EQUIVALENT. The first input/check poll precedes all work.
    - R15 the 44-byte membership input charge: accounting only and unpinned by any test. An input-budget edge
      over membership would pin it.

Findings A
- A-F1 [MEDIUM — design incoherence, implementation follows one side. Resolve before any creation writer signs
  `unavailable`.]
  - The codec has two rules that contradict each other:
    - codec :165-166: "wrong length/hash produces corrupt entries".
    - codec :406-408, the governing checkpoint: "A hash-valid request that fails its writer signature or exact
      manifest binding is invalid member evidence, not a repairable missing-byte condition".
  - The code folds the length check into byte validity (:447-449). It never reaches writer/manifest
    verification for a hash-valid object whose issuer-signed length is false.
  - RP14a shows genuine original request bytes reported as Corrupt, with the member accepted. The fault is
    attributed to the raw bytes, not to the false signed metadata.
  - Consequences:
    - A future observer would sign an `unavailable: corrupt` statement about authentic bytes.
    - The coordinate can never be restored, since any CID-matching candidate has the "wrong" length.
  - No false completion or publication is possible: there is no consumer, and publication re-verifies.
  - Same class, also accepted as a loss:
    - RP14b, an empty-CID with a positive signed length.
    - Signed lengths above evidence_service MAX_REQUEST (2 MiB + 4 KiB, src/evidence_service.rs:14-15), which no
      valid service request can have.
  - Required: decide which rule governs. For hash-valid bytes with a disagreeing authenticated length, refusing
    as invalid member evidence matches the checkpoint text and the north star (do not misattribute raw data).
    Then pin it in both implementations.
- A-F2 [LOW-MEDIUM — authentication gap in a reported projection]
  - Partial profile-3 membership is unauthenticated: the plan digest needs every source commit (RP02;
    copied.rs:200-203 has the same property).
  - Member.losses() nevertheless emits null coordinates and expected lengths derived from it.
  - The only signal is recipe_metadata_complete()==false. The loss entries themselves do not say which
    coordinates are authenticated.
  - Codec :103-105 says expectedLength comes "from authenticated metadata/membership".
  - Partial members cannot publish in KNB1, but a creation writer would still sign these coordinates.
  - Required before creation:
    - EITHER mark membership-only coordinates in partial members as unauthenticated, or withhold them,
    - OR state in the design that partial-copy membership is attested only by the external copy job.
- A-F3 [LOW — early-detectable impossibility deferred]: shared request CIDs across distinct (writer, op)
  occurrences (RP03) are accepted when the bytes are missing.
  - Static service requests make this unsatisfiable: the request bytes fix one operation and position.
  - Codec :157-158 deliberately keeps per-occurrence coordinates, and the Member claims no recoverability, so
    this is consistent but weak.
  - Consider refusing it outright for the service-request payload profile.
- A-F4 [LOW — test pinning]
  - The author suite does not pin these guards:
    - early/prompt cancellation (the retained survivor)
    - historical receipt issuer
    - source tip
    - plan scope/issuer binding
    - static writer
    - null coordinates for unreferenced membership keys
    - partial retained-membership
    - writer predecessor without bytes
    - empty-CID orphan
    - chunked member hashing
  - Production code is correct on each (probes above). Promote RP01, RP04-RP07, RP09, RP10a, RP15-RP17
    (deterministic), and keep RP10b/RP10d as recorded timing evidence. A deterministic member-stage hook,
    analogous to scope B's, would replace them.
- A-F5 [INFO]
  - Redundant/equivalent guards: R03, R14, R18 (layered).
  - Unpinned accounting: R15.
  - Membership length 0 refuses with the label "forensic-recovery-required" (:207-211). The refusal is
    correct; the label is misleading.
  - The caller duty to refuse non-canonical physical CID text lives only in the design (codec :389-390), not in
    the module rustdoc. The DASL parser itself refuses uppercase (RP13).

Scope-narrowing (Step 4): the diff's "remain separate work" / "pending" lines (codec :412-414, :417-422) defer
greedy partitioning, replay, checkpoints, schema and storage. Those were named BEFORE this checkpoint (codec
:305-310), so the deferral is legitimate, not drift. No other narrowing language was found
(logs/32-scope-narrowing-grep.txt, which also records the 99f1fba src/ diffstat and the empty merge diff).
Forbidden patterns:
- No store mutation, subject destruction, blocking hook, second UI or cites manipulation.
- Persistence surface unchanged, so no read-write-surface.tsv obligation.
- Raw corrupt/empty/orphan bytes are retained verbatim in M1. A-F1 is a mis-projection, not a collapse of raw
  data.

REQUIREMENT TABLE — Scope A (checkpoint: codec "Next verifier checkpoint", :384-422)

CK1 — Pure verifier over owner context and borrowed ordered slices; not an opener; no SQLite or storage
writer.
- Verdict: met.
- Evidence: src :1-2, :76-82; no fs/rusqlite in the module; lib.rs:32 is the only reference.

CK2 — Caller acquires bounded slices and refuses non-canonical CID text before typed CIDs.
- Verdict: unverifiable here (caller duty).
- Evidence: the typed API cannot see spellings. RP13 shows the parser refuses uppercase. There is no rustdoc
  (A-F5).

CK3 — Item, input-byte, time and cancellation limits bound the invocation.
- Verdict: met.
- Evidence: :132-167; RP10a-d, RP11; A-item/input/cancelled; R12/R13.

CK4 — Stores only bounded coordinates; never copies payloads.
- Verdict: met.
- Evidence: :199-206 (Cid, length, flags, index). The plan is the only copied blob (≤4096 bytes).

- Verdict: met.
- Evidence: :168-174, :411, :459. RP10d is 1.15 ms worst case; R12/R13 are killed.

CK6 — Contiguous issuer chain.
- Verdict: met.
- Evidence: :305, :308-319 → evidence_attestation.rs:277-301. RP12; wrong-owner-archive vector.

CK7 — Admitted vs retained purpose.
- Verdict: met.
- Evidence: :320-331. RP07; R07 is killed.

CK8 — Static service writer form.
- Verdict: met.
- Evidence: :344-354. RP09; R10 is killed (by the reviewer only).

CK9 — Per-writer position and predecessor.
- Verdict: met.
- Evidence: :355-364. RP17; R09 is semantic only with RP17.

CK10 — Unique operation.
- Verdict: met.
- Evidence: :366-369. A-duplicate-operation.

CK11 — Operation-to-slot commitment and consistent slot bindings.
- Verdict: met (slot); the binding check is redundant.
- Evidence: :386-397. R04 is killed; R03 is equivalent.

CK12 — Profile 3 binds plan, membership and retained-prefix digest.
- Verdict: partial.
- Evidence: the plan is bound by the archive ID (:263-269) plus R11/RP06. The digest is checked when complete
  (:421-425). For partial copies, membership is unauthenticated (RP02, A-F2).

CK13 — An unfinished prefix is reported incomplete; missing writer signatures are not certified.
- Verdict: met.
- Evidence: recipe_metadata_complete (:413-429); verified_requests counts only Available occurrences.

CK14 — No standalone publication capability.
- Verdict: met.

CK15 — Every known length is positive, ≤4 MiB, and agrees across references and membership.
- Verdict: met.

- Verdict: met.

Remaining parent work is unimplemented and must NOT be rounded up. The parent design is
.design/kan-v2-recovery-bundles.md:

- AC-2 observation fixtures: PARTIAL. The observation wire was qualified at an earlier checkpoint; source and
  output commitments are framing-only; there is no replay.
- AC-3 missing/corrupt/restored distinct through backup/rebuild/publication: UNMET. This checkpoint only
  distinguishes original loss logically.
- AC-4 crash boundaries: UNMET. AC-5 refusals without rewriting: UNMET at the storage level. AC-6 fresh review
  with ledger-omission/overwrite/early-completion/downgrade controls: UNMET.
- REQ-7 bounded materialization: PARTIAL, for this pure call only.
- Still to build:
  - greedy signed-loss partition into ≤32-entry / 16 KiB `unavailable` events
  - full observation replay
  - R1 historical candidate selection
  - O1 output revalidation and publication-intent/observed/failed rules
  - external checkpoints
  - physical KNB1 DDL, opener, UTF-8 gate and schema reader that refuses non-canonical CID text
  - creation, restoration and publication writers with crash tests

SCOPE A VERDICT: **APPROVE WITH FOLLOW-UPS**
The verifier is a sound, bounded, pure checkpoint. Every guard I attacked either refuses correctly or is a
demonstrated equivalent. Cancellation and deadlines are prompt, and the M1/loss output matches an independent
signed construction. It confers no history, recoverability or publication authority. It is not BLOCK because
nothing consumes it and no invariant is violated.
Required before creation signs `unavailable` events:
- A-F1 is a real contradiction in the governing text, and the code currently mislabels authentic bytes as
  corrupt under false signed lengths.
- A-F2 leaves partial-copy loss coordinates unauthenticated without saying so per entry.
A-F3 and A-F4 are test/design hardening. The early-cancellation author survivor is retained. It is now
semantically pinned only by reviewer probes, not by the author suite.

=====================================================================================================
B. FRAMING FOLLOW-THROUGH (99f1fba)

- No non-test runtime change: CONFIRMED.
  - `git diff 61b8667 99f1fba -- src/` is +76/-0, in evidence_recovery_commitment.rs only.
  - Every added runtime line is #[cfg(test)]: the field (:71-72), the initialiser (:91-92), the injection
    block in Meter::check (:98-105) and the test module (:418+).
  - The non-test lib compiles under all-target clippy (logs/04, logs/92), so no non-test path names the field.
  - The merge 88db7c9 did not touch member code: `git diff 3169a0a 5e54513` on the member src/test is empty.
- RA3/RA4 promotion is FAITHFUL: whitespace-normalised token streams equal the original reviewer functions,
  and the helpers are identical apart from emit, which now writes to stderr (logs/30).
- Polling units are meaningful, deterministic evidence of bounded interruption granularity:
  - They drive the real MemberFraming::original_object and RestorationFraming::candidate.
  - They inject cancellation when charged bytes reach a threshold, with no sleeps and no host-speed skip.
  - They assert exact charged deltas (60 + 65536 and 65536) and poisoning.
- The 13 follow-up controls, reproduced from the tracked reviewer-cases.json (cmd/controls_b.py,
  mutations/scope-b/, logs/40):
  - All 13 are KILLED by semantic assertions.
  - AC01: left Ok(()) vs Err(Cancelled). AC02: 4194304 vs 65536 charged.
  - AC25: both units fail.
  - AC03–AC08, AC16, AC17: out-of-bound input accepted (true vs false).
  - AC09 and AC10: "must refuse".
- Reviewer additions:
  - RB1/RB2 (poll every 128 KiB instead of 64 KiB) are KILLED: 131132 vs 65596 and 131072 vs 65536. The units
    pin the stated granularity, not just "some" polling.
  - RB4 (put's leading check removed) SURVIVED. It is equivalent: per-chunk spend checks remain.
  - RB3 (issuer bound counted in chars instead of bytes) SURVIVED. Rust has no multibyte edge test.
- Python issuer bound: a char-count mutant of recovery_commitments.py is killed by its new é×41 check, with
  "accepted invalid issuer byte length" (logs/31; attempt 1 failed on a root path and is retained).
- The codec now states the issuer rule as 1..80 UTF-8 bytes (codec :56-58), with canonical DID as a stricter
  member rule.
- UTF-8 create/open is explicitly "a proposed format requirement; no creation/opener exists yet" (:10-13). It
  is not an implemented gate.
- O1 confers no output authority (:378-381; module doc :1-5). The member verifier computes only Domain::Member.

Findings B
- B-F1 [LOW]: the Rust framing has no multibyte issuer edge, so RB3 survives. Add 'é'×40 accepted and
  'é'×41 refused to rv_a4.
- B-F2 [LOW/INFO]: the polling units prove same-thread poll granularity in charged bytes. They do not prove
  deadline polling, which still has only the original timing probe (prior A-F4), or cross-thread wall-clock
  latency. My RP10b/d supply the latter for the member stage only.
- B-F3 [INFO]: the regression file header (tests/evidence_recovery_commitment_review_regressions.rs:3-4) says
  "Vectors come from review-evidence/probes/indep_commitments.py". RA3/RA4 use no vectors, and the path is
  relative to a different review. Stale provenance text.

REQUIREMENT TABLE — Scope B
- B1 RA3/RA4 promoted: met (logs/30, baseline).
- B2 deterministic polling, no production hook, real operations: met (cfg(test) sites; units; AC01/02/25,
  RB1/RB2).
- B3 13 controls fail assertions: met, reproduced (logs/40).
- B4 issuer 1..80 UTF-8 bytes explicit plus Python edges: met (codec :56-58; logs/31). Rust multibyte edge
  missing (B-F1).
- B5 UTF-8 create/open a proposal only: met as a statement; not implemented, correctly so labelled.
- B6 O1 grants no authority: met.
- B7 no non-test runtime change: met.

SCOPE B VERDICT: **APPROVE WITH FOLLOW-UPS** (B-F1 and B-F3 are trivial; B-F2 restates the prior A-F4 limit
for deadlines).

=====================================================================================================
PRESERVED FAILED ATTEMPTS
- logs/10 (…ATTEMPT1) and logs/11 (…ATTEMPT2): probe construction errors.
  - proof::issue refuses `admitted` over historical receipts.
  - The record schema refuses non-static did:key, did:web+versionId and did:plc+event writers.
  - Fixed in logs/12.

- I did not rerun the 35+ historical commitment controls or the Node/performance/compatibility matrices, as

def pack(name,m,observer,error=None,complete=True):
    out={'name':name,'context':{'bundle':'01'*32,'profile':m['profile'],'archive':m['archive'].hex(),'scope':m['scope'].hex(),'issuer':m['issuer'],'observer':observer},'plan':None if m['plan'] is None else m['plan'].hex(),'membership':m['membership'],'records':[[seq,a.hex(),b.hex(),c.hex()] for seq,a,b,c in m['records']],'objects':[[c,b.hex()] for c,b in m['objects']]}
    if error:out['error']=error
    else:
        loss,available=losses(m);out['expected']={'member':framing.member_digest(m).hex(),'losses':loss,'verifiedRequests':available,'recipeMetadataComplete':complete,'through':len(m['records'])}
    return out

def vectors():
    cases=[]
    for p in [2,3]:
        for n in [0,3]:
            m,o=build(p,n);cases.append(pack(f'profile{p}-{n}-intact',m,o))
        m,o=build(p,3);m['objects'].pop(0);m['objects'][0][1]=b'';m['objects'].append([framing.raw_cid(b'orphan'),b'broken']);m['objects'].sort();cases.append(pack(f'profile{p}-loss',m,o))
    m,o=build(3,3);m['records']=m['records'][:1];cases.append(pack('partial-profile3',m,o,complete=False))
    def negative(name,profile,edit,reason):
        m,o=build(profile,2);edit(m);cases.append(pack(name,m,o,reason))
    negative('wrong-owner-archive',2,lambda m:m.update(archive=b'\x09'*32),'issuer proof')
    negative('absent-original-membership',3,lambda m:m.update(membership=[]),'retained reference absent from membership')
    negative('conflicting-membership-length',3,lambda m:m['membership'][0].__setitem__(1,m['membership'][0][1]+1),'conflicting expected lengths')
    negative('binary-or-reversed-object-order',2,lambda m:m['objects'].reverse(),'CID order or duplicate')
    negative('duplicate-original-object',2,lambda m:m['objects'].insert(0,m['objects'][0]),'CID order or duplicate')
    negative('reordered-record',2,lambda m:m['records'].reverse(),'record position')
    negative('wrong-plan-binding',3,lambda m:m.update(archive=b'\x09'*32),'plan binding')
    negative('retained-purpose-profile2',2,lambda m:resign(m,'retained-verified'),'proof purpose')
    def bad_digest(m):
        p=codec.decode(m['plan']);p['sourceDigest']=b'\xff'*32;m['plan']=cbor(p);m['archive']=hashlib.sha256(b'tools.kan.archive.copy-plan.v1\0'+m['plan']).digest();resign(m)
    negative('resigned-false-copy-source',3,bad_digest,'source metadata digest')
    # Independently pin the corrected projection rules; these are not merely
    # hand-labelled hostile inputs. The loss oracle must refuse each contradiction.
    def contradiction(name,m,o,reason):
        try:losses(m)
        except ValueError as e:assert str(e)==reason
        else:raise AssertionError(name+' accepted by projection oracle')
        cases.append(pack(name,m,o,reason))
    def edit_manifest(m,index,edit):
        rec=codec.decode(m['records'][index][1]);edit(rec['body']);raw=cbor(rec)
        receipt=codec.decode(m['records'][index][2]);receipt['body']['manifest']=codec.Link(codec.cid_bytes(codec.cid(raw)))
        m['records'][index][1]=raw;m['records'][index][2]=cbor(receipt);resign(m)
    m,o=build(2,1)
    edit_manifest(m,0,lambda b:b['entries'][0].update(length=b['entries'][0]['length']+1))
    contradiction('hash-valid-false-authenticated-length',m,o,'hash-valid bytes contradict authenticated length')
    m,o=build(2,1);empty=framing.raw_cid(b'')
    edit_manifest(m,0,lambda b:b['entries'][0].update(ciphertext=codec.Link(codec.cid_bytes(empty)),length=1));m['objects']=[[empty,b'']]
    contradiction('empty-cid-false-authenticated-length',m,o,'hash-valid bytes contradict authenticated length')
    m,o=build(2,1);edit_manifest(m,0,lambda b:b['entries'][0].update(length=2*1024*1024+4097));m['objects']=[]
    contradiction('unrepresentable-service-request-length',m,o,'service request length')
    m,o=build(2,2);e=codec.decode(m['records'][0][1])['body']['entries'][0]
    edit_manifest(m,1,lambda b:b['entries'][0].update(ciphertext=e['ciphertext'],length=e['length']));m['objects']=[]
    contradiction('reused-missing-service-request',m,o,'reused service request CID')
    m,o=build(3,3);m['records']=m['records'][:1]
    fabricated=framing.raw_cid(b'not authenticated source membership');m['membership'].append([fabricated,77]);m['membership'].sort()
    cases.append(pack('partial-membership-fabrication-remains-unverified',m,o,complete=False))
    m,o=build(3,3);m['records']=m['records'][:1]
    referenced=codec.decode(m['records'][0][1])['body']['entries'][0]['ciphertext'].raw
    for cidlength in m['membership']:
        if codec.cid_bytes(cidlength[0])!=referenced:cidlength[1]+=1
    cases.append(pack('partial-membership-length-does-not-corrupt-valid-bytes',m,o,complete=False))
    return {'status':'independent signed construction and M1/loss oracle; no complete second member validator','publicPrivateScalars':[3,4,5,6],'cases':cases}

def main():
    p=argparse.ArgumentParser();p.add_argument('--write',action='store_true');p.add_argument('--check',action='store_true');a=p.parse_args();v=vectors()
    if a.write:PATH.write_text(json.dumps(v,indent=2)+'\n')
    if a.check:assert json.loads(PATH.read_text())==v
    print(f"{len(v['cases'])} independently constructed member cases; all constructed issuer chains independently verified; no full verifier claim")
if __name__=='__main__':main()

80	A later format for oversized forensic fragments needs a separate explicit recipe;
81	it must not silently truncate a row to fit M1.
82	
83	M1 intentionally excludes rebuildable indexes/lookup columns, bundle identity,
84	observations and restoration candidates. Those are bound by their own signed
85	context/history. Identical member evidence in two physical bundles has the same
86	M1. The source metadata frontier includes both manifest and issuer-statement CIDs,
87	not just a high-water sequence. For empty history both are null.
88	
89	## Event bodies
90	
91	All digests below are 32 bytes; `member` uses M1, `output` uses O1, and
92	`restorations` uses R1. O1 has exactly M1 framing with the initial domain replaced
93	by ASCII `tools.kan.recovery.output.v1` followed by a zero byte. It commits to the
94	fully verified selected output rather than the original damaged member. All attempt IDs are owner-generated
95	16-byte values. A `frontier` is a closed map `{through, manifest, attestation}`
96	with both links null iff `through=0`. Nonempty links have DAG-CBOR/SHA256 codec.
97	
98	- `created`: `{recipe: 1, member: digest, frontier}`. Exactly sequence 1; no later
99	  created event. The logical metadata/proof chain must independently verify.
100	- `unavailable`: `{member: digest, entries: [...]}`. One to 32 entries, each
101	  `{occurrence, cid, expectedLength, state}`. `occurrence` is a positive member
102	  sequence or null for a staged/orphan object; `expectedLength` is an expected
103	  length from authenticated metadata or a completely verified copy recipe. It is null
104	  for an unreferenced object without an authenticated length, including membership-only
105	  coordinates in an incomplete copy. Their basis is derived from the fixed member
106	  (issuer metadata, verified copy recipe, unverified retained membership, or original
107	  object key); readers must expose that basis alongside each loss. The signed wire
108	  does not add a second, independently editable basis field. `state` is `missing` or
109	  `corrupt`. No metadata-corruption state pretends a broken proof is trustworthy.
110	- `restored`: `{member: digest, cid, length, candidate}`. `candidate` is the raw/SHA256 CID of the
111	  verified candidate and equals `cid`; length is 1..4 MiB. The target must exist
112	  in member metadata, original membership or original object keys. Any known
113	  expected lengths must agree; conflicting references refuse. Unknown orphan
114	  length is established by this verified candidate, not invented historical data.
115	- `publication-intent`: `{attempt, member: digest, restorations: digest,
116	  output: digest, frontier}`. `output` is the expected O1 of the deterministic
117	  selected standalone output, checked before signing intent. Exactly one intent
118	  per attempt ID. No path/command is trusted as signed executable routing data.
119	- `publication-observed`: `{attempt, intent, output: digest, frontier}`. `intent`
120	  cites the exact prior intent statement. `output` is O1 of the fully verified
121	  standalone output, must equal the cited intent output commitment, using selected valid objects and unchanged original metadata.
122	  It reports an observed durable output; it never records service activation.
123	- `publication-failed`: `{attempt, intent, reason}`. Closed reason enum:
124	  `source-changed`, `invalid-candidate`, `destination-conflict`, `budget`, `io`,
125	  `verification`. It makes no assertion that an output file does not exist.
126	
127	The 32-entry limit is subordinate to the 16 KiB envelope bound. Use another
128	linked observation when encoding would exceed that bound. All created/member
129	references must equal the independently recomputed original M1. Unavailable
130	entries must match the sampled original rows and authenticated expected
131	coordinates; restoration never deletes them. Restore and publication events
132	must reference the member fixed at creation, not a silently revised member.
133	
134	R1 is `SHA256(domain || N(count) || items)`, where domain is ASCII
135	`tools.kan.recovery.restorations.v1` plus zero byte, and items in canonical CID
136	text lexical order are `F(binary CID) || N(length) || F(candidate bytes)`.
137	R1 includes every candidate with a matching restored observation strictly before
138	that intent's sequence. There is no optional unsigned selection list. Each must
139	verify against its content address and all known expected lengths. A verifier
140	replays the chain to reconstruct this exact historical set; candidates appended
141	after the intent never enter its R1. A different candidate set requires a new
142	attempt and intent. This makes restart verification independent of a lost job
143	process or an externally remembered subset.
144	
145	The virtual standalone output contains exactly the union of original object
146	keys, authenticated record object references and original membership keys.
147	Every key needs verified bytes of all known expected lengths: use its verified
148	restoration candidate from this R1 set when present, otherwise its valid original
149	bytes. A still-missing/corrupt key refuses publication, including staged/orphan
150	keys. Never drop a corrupt orphan to make verification pass, add an unreferenced
151	new object, or use a candidate recorded after the intent. Recompute expected
152	output O1 from this deterministic union and unchanged records/plan/membership; both intent and
153	publication-observed must equal it and the original metadata frontier. The normal
154	standalone verifier still independently validates all signatures and profile
155	completion. A partial profile-3 member has no KNB1 publication operation; it stays
156	a retained recovery artifact until a separate metadata-extension design exists.
157	
158	## Exact initial loss coverage
159	
160	Derive one expected coordinate for each `(occurrence sequence, object CID)` in
161	member metadata. The coordinate algorithm preserves occurrences; it does not
162	collapse history by CID. The current service-request profile additionally refuses
163	a request CID referenced by two distinct occurrences: exact request bytes fix one
164	writer, operation and position, so such metadata cannot be satisfied. A future

A later format for oversized forensic fragments needs a separate explicit recipe;
it must not silently truncate a row to fit M1.

M1 intentionally excludes rebuildable indexes/lookup columns, bundle identity,
observations and restoration candidates. Those are bound by their own signed
context/history. Identical member evidence in two physical bundles has the same
M1. The source metadata frontier includes both manifest and issuer-statement CIDs,
not just a high-water sequence. For empty history both are null.

## Event bodies

All digests below are 32 bytes; `member` uses M1, `output` uses O1, and
`restorations` uses R1. O1 has exactly M1 framing with the initial domain replaced
by ASCII `tools.kan.recovery.output.v1` followed by a zero byte. It commits to the
fully verified selected output rather than the original damaged member. All attempt IDs are owner-generated
16-byte values. A `frontier` is a closed map `{through, manifest, attestation}`
with both links null iff `through=0`. Nonempty links have DAG-CBOR/SHA256 codec.

- `created`: `{recipe: 1, member: digest, frontier}`. Exactly sequence 1; no later
  created event. The logical metadata/proof chain must independently verify.
- `unavailable`: `{member: digest, entries: [...]}`. One to 32 entries, each
  `{occurrence, cid, expectedLength, state}`. `occurrence` is a positive member
  sequence or null for a staged/orphan object; `expectedLength` is an expected
  length from authenticated metadata or a completely verified copy recipe. It is null
  for an unreferenced object without an authenticated length, including membership-only
  coordinates in an incomplete copy. Their basis is derived from the fixed member
  (issuer metadata, verified copy recipe, unverified retained membership, or original
  object key); readers must expose that basis alongside each loss. The signed wire
  does not add a second, independently editable basis field. `state` is `missing` or
  `corrupt`. No metadata-corruption state pretends a broken proof is trustworthy.
- `restored`: `{member: digest, cid, length, candidate}`. `candidate` is the raw/SHA256 CID of the
  verified candidate and equals `cid`; length is 1..4 MiB. The target must exist
  in member metadata, original membership or original object keys. Any known
  expected lengths must agree; conflicting references refuse. Unknown orphan
  length is established by this verified candidate, not invented historical data.
- `publication-intent`: `{attempt, member: digest, restorations: digest,
  output: digest, frontier}`. `output` is the expected O1 of the deterministic
  selected standalone output, checked before signing intent. Exactly one intent
  per attempt ID. No path/command is trusted as signed executable routing data.
- `publication-observed`: `{attempt, intent, output: digest, frontier}`. `intent`
  cites the exact prior intent statement. `output` is O1 of the fully verified
  standalone output, must equal the cited intent output commitment, using selected valid objects and unchanged original metadata.
  It reports an observed durable output; it never records service activation.
- `publication-failed`: `{attempt, intent, reason}`. Closed reason enum:
  `source-changed`, `invalid-candidate`, `destination-conflict`, `budget`, `io`,
  `verification`. It makes no assertion that an output file does not exist.

The 32-entry limit is subordinate to the 16 KiB envelope bound. Use another
linked observation when encoding would exceed that bound. All created/member
references must equal the independently recomputed original M1. Unavailable
entries must match the sampled original rows and authenticated expected
coordinates; restoration never deletes them. Restore and publication events
must reference the member fixed at creation, not a silently revised member.

R1 is `SHA256(domain || N(count) || items)`, where domain is ASCII
`tools.kan.recovery.restorations.v1` plus zero byte, and items in canonical CID
text lexical order are `F(binary CID) || N(length) || F(candidate bytes)`.
R1 includes every candidate with a matching restored observation strictly before
that intent's sequence. There is no optional unsigned selection list. Each must
verify against its content address and all known expected lengths. A verifier
replays the chain to reconstruct this exact historical set; candidates appended
after the intent never enter its R1. A different candidate set requires a new
attempt and intent. This makes restart verification independent of a lost job
process or an externally remembered subset.

The virtual standalone output contains exactly the union of original object
keys, authenticated record object references and original membership keys.
Every key needs verified bytes of all known expected lengths: use its verified
restoration candidate from this R1 set when present, otherwise its valid original
bytes. A still-missing/corrupt key refuses publication, including staged/orphan
keys. Never drop a corrupt orphan to make verification pass, add an unreferenced
new object, or use a candidate recorded after the intent. Recompute expected
output O1 from this deterministic union and unchanged records/plan/membership; both intent and
publication-observed must equal it and the original metadata frontier. The normal
standalone verifier still independently validates all signatures and profile
completion. A partial profile-3 member has no KNB1 publication operation; it stays
a retained recovery artifact until a separate metadata-extension design exists.

## Exact initial loss coverage

Derive one expected coordinate for each `(occurrence sequence, object CID)` in
member metadata. The coordinate algorithm preserves occurrences; it does not
collapse history by CID. The current service-request profile additionally refuses
a request CID referenced by two distinct occurrences: exact request bytes fix one
writer, operation and position, so such metadata cannot be satisfied. A future

original membership key or original object key that has no occurrence reference;
never add a second null entry for a CID already represented by occurrences.
All authenticated lengths for a CID must agree or creation refuses. The expected
length is that agreed authenticated value. For membership-only keys in an

report expectedLength null. A raw original key without authenticated length also
has expectedLength null. These are observed rows, not proof of source membership;
missing or substituted rows cannot be detected until the complete recipe verifies.

corrupt entry. Hash-valid bytes with a disagreeing authenticated length refuse as
invalid member metadata; they must not be mislabeled corrupt or repairable. An
unverified membership length neither classifies original bytes nor constrains a
restoration candidate. Available entries produce no unavailable event. Non-BLOB cells refuse creation under the M1 rule.
Sort occurrence entries first by ascending numeric sequence then canonical CID
text; sort null entries last by canonical CID text. No duplicate coordinate is
allowed. The concatenation of creation's unavailable events must equal this exact
ordered loss vector: omissions, extra entries, duplicate entries, conflicting
states or altered expected lengths refuse verification.

These events occur immediately after created, before restoration/publication.
Partition greedily into the largest consecutive prefix of at most 32 entries
whose canonical signed envelope fits 16 KiB; signatures have fixed 64-byte width.
No empty event is permitted. Empty loss coverage means created alone. Verifiers

new claim that retrospectively changes the initial sample. Preserve such media

## Physical tables

All tables use the exact frozen column order; any extra table/index/trigger/view
refuses normal bundle open. DDL must be generated once by the implementation and
pinned by canonical schema fixtures before a writer is accepted.

- `bundle_identity(singleton INTEGER PRIMARY KEY CHECK(singleton=1), bundle BLOB,
  observer TEXT, profile INTEGER, archive BLOB, scope BLOB, issuer TEXT)`.
  Byte-width/profile/DID validation is mandatory on read and before writes.
- `member_records(sequence INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, manifest BLOB, receipt BLOB,
  envelope BLOB)`: sequence positive, manifest/receipt each 1..65536 bytes,
  envelope 1..16384 bytes; all NOT NULL. No ordinary `commits` or `attestations`
  table exists in this outer format.
- `member_objects(cid TEXT PRIMARY KEY, bytes BLOB NOT NULL) WITHOUT ROWID`:

- `member_membership(cid TEXT PRIMARY KEY, length INTEGER NOT NULL) WITHOUT ROWID`:

- `observations(sequence INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, envelope BLOB NOT NULL)`:

- `restored_objects(cid TEXT PRIMARY KEY, bytes BLOB NOT NULL) WITHOUT ROWID`:

"""Reviewer-run compiled controls for the b11cbf4 correction round.

usage: python3 mutate.py <export_root> <manifest.json> [case ...]
Each case replaces exactly one anchored source string, runs the author suites plus the
temporarily placed reviewer probe file with --no-fail-fast, restores the exact bytes and
checks the restored sha256 against the frozen manifest. Logs: review-evidence/mutations/.
"""
import hashlib
import json
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(sys.argv[1]).resolve()
MANIFEST = json.load(open(sys.argv[2]))["files"]
ONLY = set(sys.argv[3:])
OUT = ROOT / "review-evidence/mutations"
MEMBER = "src/evidence_recovery_member.rs"
FRAME = "src/evidence_recovery_commitment.rs"
AUTHOR = [
    "evidence_recovery_member",
    "evidence_recovery_member_review_regressions",
    "evidence_recovery_member_corrections",
    "evidence_recovery_commitment_review_regressions",
]
PROBES = "zz_corrections_review_probes"

CASES = [
    # (name, origin, file, old, new)
    ("M01-authenticated-length", "author", MEMBER,
     "!hash_valid || c.length.is_none_or(|n| n == object.bytes.len() as u64)",
     "true || !hash_valid || c.length.is_none_or(|n| n == object.bytes.len() as u64)"),
    ("M02-partial-length-kept", "author", MEMBER,
     "if !c.referenced {", "if false && !c.referenced {"),
    ("M03-partial-basis-verified", "author", MEMBER,
     "Basis::UnverifiedMembership\n", "Basis::VerifiedCopyRecipe\n"),
    ("M04-shared-request-allowed", "author", MEMBER,
     'require(!c.referenced, "reused service request CID")?;',
     'require(true || !c.referenced, "reused service request CID")?;'),
    ("M05-request-bound-removed", "author", MEMBER,
     "n <= service::MAX_REQUEST as u64", "true || n <= service::MAX_REQUEST as u64"),
    ("M06-request-bound-off-by-one", "reviewer", MEMBER,
     "n <= service::MAX_REQUEST as u64", "n < service::MAX_REQUEST as u64"),
    ("M07-clear-referenced-too", "reviewer", MEMBER,
     "if !c.referenced {", "if true {"),
    ("M08-clear-in-complete-copies", "reviewer", MEMBER,
     "if !recipe_metadata_complete {\n        for c in keys.values_mut()",
     "if true {\n        for c in keys.values_mut()"),
    ("M09-orphan-basis-as-membership", "reviewer", MEMBER,
     "basis: if !c.member {", "basis: if false && !c.member {"),
    ("M10-length-check-on-all-bytes", "reviewer", MEMBER,
     "!hash_valid || c.length.is_none_or(|n| n == object.bytes.len() as u64)",
     "c.length.is_none_or(|n| n == object.bytes.len() as u64)"),
    ("M11-occurrence-basis-as-recipe", "reviewer", MEMBER,
     "basis: Basis::IssuerMetadata,", "basis: Basis::VerifiedCopyRecipe,"),
    ("M12-issuer-utf8-chars", "author", FRAME,
     "!header.issuer.is_empty() && header.issuer.len() <= 80",
     "!header.issuer.is_empty() && header.issuer.chars().count() <= 80"),
]


def sha(p):
    return hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def summarise(log):
    per = {}
    current = None
    for line in log.splitlines():
        m = re.search(r"Running tests/(\w+)\.rs", line)
        if m:
            current = m.group(1)
            per.setdefault(current, [])
        m = re.match(r"test (\S+) \.\.\. FAILED", line)
        if m and current:
            per[current].append(m.group(1))
    return per


def main():
    OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    originals = {f: (ROOT / f).read_bytes() for f in [MEMBER, FRAME]}
    for f, b in originals.items():
        assert hashlib.sha256(b).hexdigest() == MANIFEST[f], f + " not at frozen bytes before run"
    summary = []
    try:
        for name, origin, f, old, new in CASES:
            if ONLY and name not in ONLY:
                continue
            src = originals[f].decode()
            assert src.count(old) == 1, (name, src.count(old))
            (ROOT / f).write_text(src.replace(old, new))
            cmd = ["cargo", "test", "--offline", "--features", "v2-crypto", "--no-fail-fast"]
            for t in AUTHOR + [PROBES]:
                cmd += ["--test", t]
            r = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=900)
            log = r.stdout + r.stderr
            (OUT / (name + ".txt")).write_text(
                f"# origin={origin} file={f}\n# old={old!r}\n# new={new!r}\n# cmd={' '.join(cmd)}\n"
                + log + f"\n# exit={r.returncode}\n")
            (ROOT / f).write_bytes(originals[f])
            assert sha(ROOT / f) == MANIFEST[f], name + " restore mismatch"
            compile_fail = "could not compile" in log
            per = summarise(log)
            author_fail = {k: v for k, v in per.items() if k != PROBES and v}
            probe_fail = per.get(PROBES, [])
            line = (f"{name} [{origin}] exit={r.returncode} compile_fail={compile_fail} "
                    f"author_failures={json.dumps(author_fail)} reviewer_probe_failures={json.dumps(probe_fail)}")
            print(line, flush=True)
            summary.append(line)
    finally:
        for f, b in originals.items():
            (ROOT / f).write_bytes(b)
        for f in originals:
            assert sha(ROOT / f) == MANIFEST[f], f + " final restore mismatch"
    (OUT / "SUMMARY.txt").write_text("\n".join(summary) + "\nall sources restored to frozen sha256\n")
    print("all sources restored to frozen sha256")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Python oracle. UTF-8 is pinned for future physical creation and opening. An O1
digest from the framing builder alone still authenticates no output bytes:
full object/writer/profile verification must precede publication. None of these
changes accepts the physical format or closes parent acceptance criteria.

## Next verifier checkpoint: logical member and initial availability

The pure member verifier takes an owner-pinned context and borrowed, ordered
record, membership and original-object slices. Its caller must acquire those
bytes with bounded reads before calling; this is not a SQLite opener. The physical
reader must reject noncanonical original CID text before constructing typed CIDs;
parsing a spelling and silently normalizing it is not source validation. Explicit
item/input-byte/time/cancellation limits bound this invocation. It stores only
bounded metadata coordinates, never copies the whole payload collection. Hashing
polls per 64 KiB; canonical decoding, request verification and signatures are
individually bounded operations with cancellation checks around them.

Independently verify the contiguous issuer chain, admitted versus retained-copy
purpose, static service writer form, per-writer position/predecessor, unique
operation, the service operation-to-slot commitment and consistent slot bindings. Profile 3 additionally binds its plan,
original membership and retained-prefix metadata digest. An unfinished prefix is
reported as incomplete; matching metadata alone does not certify missing writer
signatures or retained bytes. No standalone publication capability is returned.

Every retained length must be positive, at most 4 MiB, and agree across references
and original membership; referenced service requests additionally cannot exceed
the service MAX_REQUEST bound. Contradictory shared service-request CIDs refuse
even with no payloads present. Retain raw corrupt/empty originals in M1. Verify each
present object's hash once and sample every occurrence separately; unreferenced
membership/original keys receive null-occurrence loss coordinates. A hash-valid
request that fails its writer signature or exact manifest binding is invalid
member evidence, not a repairable missing-byte condition. Missing/corrupt requests
remain unavailable, with writer verification still outstanding. Loss output is
strict occurrence/CID-text order, followed by null coordinates in CID-text order.

This checkpoint must be qualified before it can feed full observation replay.
Greedy signed-loss partitioning, historical restoration/output selection, replay,
checkpoints, physical schema and all storage mutations remain separate work.

"""Re-summarise mutation logs by `panicked at tests/<file>.rs:<line>` plus the panic message.
(mutate.py's inline summary mis-attributed failures because cargo prints `Running` on stderr.)
usage: python3 summarise.py <mutations_dir>
"""
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

d = Path(sys.argv[1])
for log in sorted(d.glob("[MW]*.txt")):
    text = log.read_text()
    head = text.splitlines()[0] if text else ""
    compile_fail = "could not compile" in text
    exit_m = re.search(r"# exit=(\d+)", text)
    print(f"== {log.stem} {head} exit={exit_m.group(1) if exit_m else '?'} compile_fail={compile_fail}")
    lines = text.splitlines()
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        m = re.search(r"thread '([^']+)' .*panicked at tests/(\w+)\.rs:(\d+)", line)
        if m:
            msg = " | ".join(l.strip() for l in lines[i + 1:i + 4] if l.strip() and not l.startswith("note:"))
            origin = "REVIEWER-PROBE" if m.group(2).startswith("zz_") else "author-suite"
            print(f"   [{origin}] {m.group(2)}::{m.group(1)} @{m.group(3)} :: {msg[:300]}")
    if compile_fail:
        for line in lines:
            if line.startswith("error"):
                print("   COMPILE " + line[:200])
